meta.title: Access Bank CPG – Consolidated Question Bank (2024 Verified)
meta.description: All questions from original JSON, HTML interactive quiz, and the new module files – deduplicated and corrected against the 2024 CPG manual. 714 unique questions across 12 modules.

modules.title: Module 1: Types of Risk & Risk Management Philosophy
Module 2: Committees, Approval Authority & Related Policies
Module 3: One Obligor Limit, Exposure (OSUC) & Risk Rating Limit Exceptions
Module 4: Core Lending Products (Term Loan, Revolving Credit, Overdraft, Lease, Warehouse)
Module 5: Bonds & Guarantees, Loan Syndication, Agricultural Loans & Cash Collateral
Module 6: Delinquency Management, Asset Classification, Provisioning & Recovery
Module 7: Foundational Policy Principles, Credit Process, Collateral & Credit Audit
Module 8: Export Finance, Product Programs, Off‑Balance Sheet Facilities, Commercial Papers, LCs, CORR & Governance
Module 9: Annual Review Types, Collateral Insurance & Foundational Credit Principles
Module 11: Environmental and Social Risk Management (ESRM)

questionBank.q: Settlement risk occurs when there is a simultaneous exchange of value with a counter party for the same value date and verification that payment is received is not made until after the bank has paid / delivered on the obligation
While considering settlement risk, there is also a risk that the counter party does not deliver at all and as such resulting in exposure of the bank to direct lending risk
questionBank.exp: Section 3.5.5 continues: 'There is a risk that the counter party does not deliver as such resulting in exposure of the bank to direct lending risk.' Confirmed True.

questionBank.q: Clearing risk is the risk that the bank may be reimbursed on another value date for payments made on behalf of customers
questionBank.exp: Section 3.5.6 (Clearing Risk) now reads: 'Clearing risk is the risk that the bank may NOT be reimbursed on the SAME value date for payments made on behalf of customers.' This is the logical equivalent of the original phrasing ('reimbursed on another/later date' = 'not reimbursed on the same date') – the concept and the True answer both still hold.

questionBank.q: Documentation risk is the risk that documentary evidence on which the bank depends to enforce rights under contracts or transactions will not be complete, covered and enforceable
questionBank.exp: Section 3.5.12 (mislabelled 3.2.12 in the current manual) reads: 'Documentary risk is the risk that documentary evidence on which the bank depends to enforce rights under contracts or transactions may not be complete, correct or enforceable.' Close paraphrase, same substance – confirmed True.

questionBank.q: Legal and regulatory risks may occur when the Bank, a related corporate entity, a transaction or a customer is subject to a change in exposure resulting from legal or criminal sanctions or litigations
questionBank.exp: Section 3.5.13 now reads: 'Legal and regulatory risk occurs when the bank, a related corporate entity (such as nonbank subsidiary or affiliate), a transaction or a customer is subject to a change in exposure resulting from regulatory, civil or criminal approvals, or litigation.' Wording updated slightly but the tested statement remains True.

questionBank.q: Liquidity risk is the risk that the bank will be able to meet all of its financial commitments to customers and markets when due
questionBank.exp: Section 3.5.9 defines liquidity risk as: 'Liquidity risk is risk that the bank may be UNABLE to meet its financial commitments to customers or markets when due.' The statement describes the opposite – so False.

questionBank.q: Contingent lending risks may occur in products ranging from letters of credit to guarantees to unusual commitments
questionBank.exp: Section 3.5.1.4 lists the product range as 'letters of credits to guarantees to unused loan commitments' – the current manual says 'unused loan commitments,' not 'unusual commitments.' The overall statement (that contingent lending risk spans these product types) remains True.

questionBank.q: Direct lending risk exists for the entire life a transaction
questionBank.exp: Section 3.5.1 (Direct Lending Risks): 'It exists for the entire life of the transaction.' Confirmed True.

questionBank.q: Direct lending risk exists only at the commencement of the credit extension
questionBank.exp: Directly contradicted by section 3.5.1, which states direct lending risk exists for the entire life of the transaction, not only at commencement. False.

questionBank.q: Direct lending risk is the risk that actual customer obligation and contingent obligations will not be repaid on time
questionBank.exp: Section 3.5.1 defines direct lending risk as concerning only 'actual customer obligations.' Contingent obligations belong to the separately defined Contingent Lending Risk (3.5.1.4). Folding contingent obligations into the direct lending risk definition conflates the two risk types, so this statement is False.

questionBank.q: Contingent lending risk exists for the entire life of the transaction
questionBank.exp: Section 3.5.1.4: 'It exists for the entire life of the transaction.' Confirmed True.

questionBank.q: Contingent lending risk is the risk that potential customer obligation will become actual obligation and will not be repaid on time
questionBank.exp: Section 3.5.1.4: 'Contingent lending risk is the risk that potential customer obligations will become actual obligations and will not be repaid on time.' Confirmed True.

questionBank.q: Country risk events may include political events
questionBank.exp: Section 3.5.14: 'Country Risk events may include sovereign defaults, currency convertibility and/or transferability restrictions, or political events.' Confirmed True.

questionBank.q: Country risk is the risk that an event in a country will impair the value of the Bank's assets or will adversely affect the ability of obligors within that country to honor their obligation to the Bank
questionBank.exp: Confirmed against section 3.5.14 verbatim: 'It is the risk that an event in a country ... will impair the value of Access Bank assets or will adversely affect the ability of obligors within that country to honour their obligations to Access Bank.'

questionBank.q: Equity risk occurs when the bank invests in, holds or receives equity, equity-like securities or other junior securities in non-affiliated entities
questionBank.exp: Confirmed verbatim against section 3.5.7 (Equity Risk). True.

questionBank.q: Fiduciary risk occurs when the bank is charged with the responsibilities of acting as a trustee for third parties
questionBank.exp: Section 3.5.10: 'Fiduciary risk occurs when the bank is charged with the responsibility of acting as a trustee for third parties.' Confirmed True.

questionBank.q: Disclosure risk is the risk that there is disclosure of information that the bank knows or should have known to be incorrect, or fails to disclose actual or potential conflicts of interest or material information
questionBank.exp: Confirmed against section 3.5.11: 'The risk is that there is disclosure of information that the bank either knows or should have known to be incorrect, that the bank does not disclose actual or potential conflicts of interest, or that the bank does not disclose or delay in disclosing material information.' True.

questionBank.q: Pre-settlement risk is the risk of default on a contractual obligation before settlement of the contract by a counter party in a transaction
questionBank.exp: Confirmed verbatim against section 3.5.3 (Pre-settlement Risk). True.

questionBank.q: Price risk is the risk that market conditions may change for an individual instrument or for all securities of the same general class
questionBank.exp: Confirmed verbatim against section 3.5.8 (Price Risk). True.

questionBank.q: Access Bank's risk appetite is moderate and guarded
questionBank.exp: Section 3.2 (Risk Management Philosophy): 'the Bank's Risk Management philosophy is that moderate and guarded risk attitude will ensure sustainable growth in shareholder value and reputation.' Confirmed True.

questionBank.q: The Bank's Risk Management philosophy is that a moderate and guarded risk attitude will ensure sustainable growth in shareholder value and reputation

According to the Bank's Risk Management Philosophy, the Bank considers risk management philosophy and culture as the set of shared beliefs, values, attitudes and practices characterizing how the Bank considers risk in everything it does
questionBank.exp: Confirmed verbatim against section 3.2: 'the Bank considers risk management philosophy and culture as the set of shared beliefs, values, attitudes and practices characterizing how the Bank considers risk in everything it does, from strategy development and implementation to its day-to-day activities.' True.

questionBank.q: Equal attention shall be paid to both quantifiable and non-quantifiable risks
questionBank.exp: Confirmed against the Bank's risk culture guiding principles (section 3.2/3.3): 'Equal attention shall be paid to both quantifiable and non-quantifiable risks.' True.

questionBank.q: The Bank shall avoid products and businesses it does not understand
questionBank.exp: Listed among the Bank's risk culture guiding principles: 'The Bank shall avoid products and businesses it does not understand.' Confirmed True.

questionBank.q: What is the risk that a counterparty to a transaction will fail to perform according to the terms and conditions of the contract, causing the holder of the claim to suffer a loss in cash flow or market value?
questionBank.exp: New question covering section 3.5.1, Counterparty Risk – definition confirmed verbatim.

questionBank.q: Where the default on one debt obligation automatically triggers the default of another debt obligation, this is known as:
questionBank.exp: New question covering section 3.5.1 (Cross Default Risk): 'Failure of one set of obligation to perform leads to the automatic declaration of other obligations to be in default.'

questionBank.q: Access Bank shall maintain a minimum leverage ratio of what percentage at all times?
questionBank.exp: New question covering section 3.5.4 (Leverage Ratio): 'Access Bank shall maintain a minimum leverage ratio of 4% at all times.'

questionBank.q: Operational risk, as defined in the CPG, refers to the risk of loss to the bank resulting from:
opts: Inadequate or failed procedures, people, systems or policies, including fraud or other criminal activity
Only fraud committed by external parties
Market price fluctuations affecting the trading book
Failure of a counterparty to deliver on a settlement date
questionBank.ans: Inadequate or failed procedures, people, systems or policies, including fraud or other criminal activity

questionBank.q: Foreign exchange rate risk refers to the risk of:
opts: Deterioration of the currency in which the borrower earns income against the currency of the Bank's exposure, adversely affecting repayment capacity
The Bank's inability to source foreign currency for its own operations
A customer defaulting solely due to an interest rate change
Fluctuation in the Bank's own share price
questionBank.ans: Deterioration of the currency in which the borrower earns income against the currency of the Bank's exposure, adversely affecting repayment capacity
questionBank.exp: New question covering section 3.5.16 (Foreign Exchange Rate Risk).

questionBank.q: Issuer risk is best described as:
opts: The risk that the market value of a security or debt instrument changes when the perceived or actual credit standing of the issuer changes
The risk that a bank employee issues a credit facility without proper authority
The risk that a bond is issued in the wrong currency
The risk that a guarantee is issued without a corresponding master facility
questionBank.ans: The risk that the market value of a security or debt instrument changes when the perceived or actual credit standing of the issuer changes

questionBank.q: The Management Credit Committee (MCC) is the highest management approval body for credits in Access Bank
questionBank.exp: Confirmed verbatim, section 4.2.1.3: 'The Management Credit Committee (MCC) is the highest management approval body for credits in Access Bank...'

questionBank.q: The Board Credit Committee is the highest credit approval body in the bank and is responsible for approval of credit beyond the authorized approval limit
questionBank.exp: False – this conflates BCC with MCC. The manual specifically reserves the phrase 'highest management approval body' for the MCC. The BCC acts on behalf of the Board of Directors but is not itself the overall highest body – that is the Board of Directors.

questionBank.q: Who chairs the Management Credit Committee, and who serves as Vice Chairman?
opts: Managing Director/CEO (Chairman); Deputy Managing Director(s) (Vice Chairman)
Group Managing Director (Chairman); Group Deputy Managing Director (Vice Chairman)
Chief Risk Officer (Chairman); Executive Director Risk (Vice Chairman)
Head of Credit Risk Management (Chairman); Group Head Legal (Vice Chairman)
questionBank.ans: Managing Director/CEO (Chairman); Deputy Managing Director(s) (Vice Chairman)
questionBank.exp: Section 4.2.1.4: 'Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer – Chairman; Deputy Managing Directors – Vice Chairman.' Updated to current titles.

questionBank.q: For an MCC meeting, the Chairman or Vice Chairman, the Secretary and at least 2 other members shall form a quorum
questionBank.exp: False as worded – the actual quorum requires a representative from Legal Department and at least two other Group Heads/Zonal Heads/Sector Heads not below AGM level, plus a Group Head/Head of Risk in CRM. Not just any '2 other members.'

questionBank.q: What is the correct quorum requirement for a valid MCC meeting?
opts: Chairman or Vice Chairman, the Secretary, a Legal Department representative, at least two Group/Zonal/Sector Heads (AGM level or above), and a Group Head/Head of Risk in CRM
Chairman or Vice Chairman and any 2 members present, regardless of role
Any 5 Group Heads, with or without the Chairman or Vice Chairman
The Managing Director alone, with ratification by circulation afterward
questionBank.ans: Chairman or Vice Chairman, the Secretary, a Legal Department representative, at least two Group/Zonal/Sector Heads (AGM level or above), and a Group Head/Head of Risk in CRM
questionBank.exp: New question testing the precise quorum from section 4.2.1.4.

questionBank.q: In the absence of the Chairman for an MCC meeting, what happens?
opts: The Vice Chairman presides, or the Chairman may delegate any Committee member to act as Chairman
The meeting is automatically cancelled and rescheduled
The Head of Credit Risk Management automatically presides
No meeting may be held without the Chairman under any circumstance
questionBank.ans: The Vice Chairman presides, or the Chairman may delegate any Committee member to act as Chairman
questionBank.exp: Section 4.2.1.4: 'For an MCC meeting to be valid, it must be presided over by the Chairman or Vice Chairman. In their absence, the Chairman may delegate any member of the Committee to act as Chairman.'

questionBank.q: The Management Credit Committee shall meet at least once a month
questionBank.exp: False – per section 4.2.1.4, the MCC meets bi-weekly for facility requests and at least once a year for policy review. 'Once a month' understates the facility-request cadence and doesn't match either stated frequency.

questionBank.q: How often does the MCC meet to review and consider facility requests, versus for CPG policy review and direction-setting purposes?
opts: Bi-weekly for facility requests; at least once a year for policy review and direction-setting
Quarterly for facility requests; bi-weekly for policy review
Only on an ad-hoc basis for both purposes
questionBank.ans: Bi-weekly for facility requests; at least once a year for policy review and direction-setting
questionBank.exp: New question drawn directly from section 4.2.1.4.

questionBank.q: It is not always necessary for members of the MCC to attend meetings in person; approvals can also be obtained by circulation of a credit memo, telephone or video conference for absent members
questionBank.exp: Confirmed, section 4.2.1.4: 'in exceptional circumstances MCC approvals may be obtained by telephone/video conference meetings or written comments and formal approval of MCC members properly captured in the MCC minutes.'

questionBank.q: The Board Credit Committee shall meet not more than once quarterly
questionBank.exp: False – this inverts the actual rule. Section 4.2.1.2.1: 'The Board Credit Committee shall meet at least once quarterly. However, special Board Credit Committee meetings may be convened...' It is a floor, not a ceiling.

questionBank.q: The composition of the Board Credit Committee and the frequency of its meetings is fully specified within the CPG manual itself
questionBank.exp: False – the manual defers to the BCC Charter: 'The composition of the Board Credit Committee and the frequency of their meeting shall be governed by the provisions in the Charter for Board Credit Committee' (section 4.2.1.2.1).

questionBank.q: The Criticized Assets Committee (CAC) is headed by the Deputy Managing Director and is convened once every month
questionBank.exp: False on both counts. Section 4.2.1.6: chaired by the 'Managing Director or his designate,' and convened 'at least once every quarter,' not monthly.

questionBank.q: Who chairs the Criticized Assets Committee, and how often does it convene?
opts: Managing Director (or designate); at least once every quarter
Head of Credit Risk Management; annually
questionBank.ans: Managing Director (or designate); at least once every quarter

questionBank.q: Facilities shall be regarded as delinquent (a 'Criticized Asset') where normal repayment of principal and/or interest is in arrears for more than 90 days but less than 360 days
The decision to transfer a non-performing facility to the remedial assets management unit is normally taken at Management Credit Committee meetings
questionBank.exp: False – this decision-making role belongs to the Criticized Assets Committee, per section 4.2.1.5's mandate to 'take decisions on remedial actions and/or provisioning,' not the MCC.

questionBank.q: In the absence of the Managing Director, the Deputy Managing Director automatically assumes the Managing Director's approval limit
questionBank.exp: False. No provision in the current manual supports automatic assumption of the MD's personal approval limit by the DMD in his/her absence – approval authority is tied to specific delegated roles.

questionBank.q: Credit approval authority shall be approved by the Managing Director/CEO based on delegation by the Board of Directors, on the recommendation of Business Executive Directors and the Chief Risk Officer
questionBank.exp: Confirmed against section 6.2.10.4.3 with updated titles.

questionBank.q: The level of authority required to approve credit will decrease as the amount and transaction risk decreases and as the risk rating improves
questionBank.exp: Consistent with the general architecture of the Credit Approval Authority Limits framework – smaller, lower-risk, better-rated exposures require lower-level approval.

questionBank.q: Risk Rating Limits are established by the Chief Risk Officer and approved by the Management Credit Committee
questionBank.exp: CORRECTION to the legacy bank – section 5.3.5 confirms this is True.

questionBank.q: Regardless of Risk Rating Limits, Legal Lending Limits set by the Regulators shall always prevail
Each customer-facing business unit need not maintain up-to-date records of credit approval authority delegated to approving officers
All appointments and designations for credit risk approval, along with corresponding credit limits, must be reviewed and re-approved by the Chief Risk Officer at least how often?
questionBank.exp: Section 6.2.10.6.1: '...must be reviewed and reapproved by the Chief Risk Officer at least once a year.'

questionBank.q: Approvals under credit programs need not be within approved global exposure and maximum individual exposure limits
questionBank.exp: CORRECTION – section 6.2.10.6.2 states the opposite: 'Approvals under credit programs shall be within approved global exposure and maximum individual exposure limits.'

questionBank.q: Amendments to credit agreements — such as lengthening tenor, increasing facility amount, or materially relaxing collateral structure — do not require full credit approval of Total Facilities under the Credit Approval Grid
questionBank.exp: False. Material amendments of this kind do trigger a full re-approval requirement under the Credit Facility Approval Authority.

questionBank.q: When an established credit facility undergoes a material change in terms, tenor or conditions, Total Facilities must be re-approved in accordance with the Credit Facility Approval Authority
questionBank.exp: Consistent with the Credit Facility Approval Grid's general re-approval trigger.

questionBank.q: There is no limit to the amount of credit which may be approved by the Board of Directors, provided the credit conforms to the CPG and statutory lending limits
questionBank.exp: True in principle – the Board sits at the apex, with Legal Lending Limits as the only hard ceiling.

questionBank.q: It is the responsibility of Management and the Board of Directors to ensure the integrity of the credit process and proper documentation of the credit decision
questionBank.exp: False as worded – this names the wrong party. Section 6.2.10.4 states: 'It is the responsibility of the Relationship Manager/Originating Officer to ensure the integrity of the credit process and the proper documentation of the credit decision.'

questionBank.q: Waivers of interest and/or credit charges require approval of which officer, and to which category of exposures is such consideration limited?
opts: The Managing Director; limited to exposures classified as lost
The Head of Credit Risk Management; available for any performing exposure
The Management Credit Committee; limited to substandard exposures only
The Relationship Manager; available at any stage of delinquency
questionBank.ans: The Managing Director; limited to exposures classified as lost
questionBank.exp: Section 8.3.2: 'All waivers of interest and charges shall require approval of the MD... Consideration of waivers... shall be limited to credit exposures classified as lost.'

questionBank.q: Release of collateral, guarantee or support requires joint approval by both the Head of Risk and the Managing Director, upon confirmation of full payment of the credit facility
questionBank.exp: CORRECTION – section 7.7.2.13 states release requires approval by the Head of Risk alone, not a joint Head of Risk + MD requirement.

questionBank.q: Unsecured loans to individuals or organisations, other than to members of staff of the Bank, shall require which approval, irrespective of the amount involved?
opts: The Managing Director's approval (MCC/BCC/Board approval may additionally be required per the approval grid)
Only the Relationship Manager's approval, regardless of amount
Only the Board of Directors' approval, with no other officer able to approve
No specific approval is required beyond ordinary facility sign-off
questionBank.ans: The Managing Director's approval (MCC/BCC/Board approval may additionally be required per the approval grid)
questionBank.exp: Section 5.2.4: 'All loans in these categories must be approved by the MD irrespective of the amount involved and Tenor (MCC/BCC/Board approval may be required in line with the bank's approval grid).'

questionBank.q: Unsecured credit to a company where a bank director is also a director, or which is owned/controlled by a close associate or relative of a bank director, requires what approval?
opts: Board approval prior to drawdown, and the loan must also be mentioned at Board Meetings for ratification
Approval by the Relationship Manager alone, given the special relationship
No special approval beyond the normal approval grid
Approval by the Chief Risk Officer alone, without Board involvement
questionBank.ans: Board approval prior to drawdown, and the loan must also be mentioned at Board Meetings for ratification

questionBank.q: Under the current (2024) Group EXCO credit approval limits, what is an Executive Director's approval limit for new credits of Standard Grade?
questionBank.exp: Current EXCO table: ED — N200mm (Standard Grade, new credits). Legacy figure N75mm is outdated.

questionBank.q: Under the current (2024) Group EXCO credit approval limits, what is the Managing Director/CEO's approval limit for new credits of Standard Grade?
questionBank.exp: Current MD/CEO limit: N800mm (Standard Grade, new credits).

questionBank.q: Under the current (2024) approval framework, are MCC, BCC and Board of Directors approval limits set as flat Naira amounts, or do they vary by obligor risk rating?
opts: They vary by obligor risk rating — higher (better) ratings carry substantially larger MCC/BCC/Board exposure limits
They are flat, fixed amounts that apply uniformly regardless of risk rating
They vary only by industry sector, not by risk rating
They are set solely by loan tenor, with risk rating playing no role
questionBank.ans: They vary by obligor risk rating — higher (better) ratings carry substantially larger MCC/BCC/Board exposure limits
questionBank.exp: The current MCC/BCC/Board limit table is risk‑rating‑banded, not flat. This is a significant change.

questionBank.q: Under the current Temporary Overdraft (TOD) approval grid, what is the Executive Director's TOD limit for Standard Grade exposures?
questionBank.exp: Current TOD grid: ED — N100mm (Standard Grade).

questionBank.q: Any Temporary Overdraft (TOD) request for a new obligor with less than 6 months' banking relationship with the Bank will require what level of approval, regardless of the amount?
opts: MCC approval, subject to the MCC limit stated in the TOD grid
Automatic decline with no approval pathway available
Relationship Manager approval only, given the small typical size of such requests
Board of Directors approval only, bypassing MCC entirely
questionBank.ans: MCC approval, subject to the MCC limit stated in the TOD grid
questionBank.exp: Confirmed from the manual immediately following the TOD table.

questionBank.q: Section 19(1a) of the Bank and Other Financial Institutions Act (BOFIA) 2020 states that a Bank shall not grant more than what percentage of its shareholders' funds unimpaired by losses to a company, its subsidiaries and associates?
questionBank.exp: Confirmed against section 5.3.2 – the percentage (20%) is unchanged but the citation is now Section 19(1a) of BOFIA 2020.

questionBank.q: Section 20 (1a) of the Banks and Other Financial Institutions Act (BOFIA) 1991 as amended states that a Bank shall not grant more than 50% of its shareholders' funds unimpaired by losses to a company, its subsidiaries and associates
questionBank.exp: False on both percentage and citation – correct is 20% and Section 19(1a) of BOFIA 2020.

questionBank.q: What concept describes the BOFIA requirement that a Bank shall not grant more than 20% of its shareholders' funds unimpaired by losses to a company, its subsidiaries and associates?
questionBank.exp: Confirmed – this is the One Obligor concept (section 5.3.2).

questionBank.q: At Access Bank, the concept of one obligor is extended to include any company belonging to a group whose management are strongly linked by virtue of their related ownership structure, particularly where the business fortune of one entity affects the other

With regard to the one obligor limit, it shall be the responsibility of the Board of Directors to determine whether related company obligations shall be aggregated, and the basis for their decision shall be documented
questionBank.exp: False – responsibility is with the Approving Officers, not the Board (section 5.3.2).

questionBank.q: As a guide, the term 'One Obligor' to a borrower includes all subsidiaries owned at least 50%, such interest to be an aggregate of both direct and indirect shareholding

As a guide, the term 'One Obligor' to a borrower includes any less-than-50%-owned affiliate where the borrower exercises management control, and where the affiliate's commercial fortunes are strongly influenced by the borrower
As a guide, the term 'One Obligor' to a borrower includes any obligor related to the borrower as a result of guarantees, endorsements, or other similar arrangements in favour of the Bank
As a guide, the term 'One Obligor' to a borrower includes all obligors under common ownership or control of a corporation or individual
When establishing Total Facilities for a relationship, credit facilities to affiliates owned between 20% and 50% (where the borrower effectively controls the affiliate) should be:
opts: Included in Total Facilities for the relationship
Always excluded from Total Facilities regardless of control
Only included if the affiliate is listed on a stock exchange
Only included with the affiliate's own separate Board approval
questionBank.ans: Included in Total Facilities for the relationship
questionBank.exp: Section 5.3.6: Total Facilities 'should also include credit facilities to affiliates (up to 20% but less than 50% owned) where the borrower effectively controls' the affiliate.

questionBank.q: At Access Bank, exposure against Risk Rating Limits is measured as the Outstandings and Unused Commitments ('OSUC') to a given relationship
OSUC is the sum of all Outstandings (including Direct and Contingent Exposure) against Total Facilities, as well as the unused portion of any Committed Facility included in Total Facilities
OSUC does not include settlement and clearing exposure, or the Underwritten Position of a credit underwriting transaction, unless the position becomes aged beyond the Extension Period

For purposes of measuring exposure against Risk Rating Limits, OSUC may be considered gross of reductions resulting from sales of assets and risk mitigation efforts restricted to on- and off-balance-sheet netting
questionBank.exp: False – section 5.3.5.1 says OSUC may be considered NET OF those items, not gross.

questionBank.q: For the purposes of applying Risk Rating Limits, which obligor risk rating is used?
opts: For corporations, the parent company's rating; for banks, the lead bank's rating; for other entities, the rating per Access Bank's Risk Rating Policy
Always the rating of the specific legal entity requesting the facility, regardless of group structure
Always the lowest (weakest) rating among all group entities
The average rating across all entities in the group
questionBank.ans: For corporations, the parent company's rating; for banks, the lead bank's rating; for other entities, the rating per Access Bank's Risk Rating Policy

questionBank.q: It is the responsibility of the Head of Credit Risk Management to ensure that actual OSUC stays within the Risk Rating Limit or is covered by an approved Risk Rating Limit exception
questionBank.exp: False – section 5.3.6: 'It is the responsibility of the Relationship Manager to ensure that actual OSUC stays within the Risk Rating Limit or is covered by an approved Risk Rating Limit exception.'

questionBank.q: Risk Rating Limit Exceptions (RRLEs) are encouraged and need not be approved in advance
questionBank.exp: False – section 5.3.5.2: 'Risk Rating Limit Exceptions are discouraged and must be approved in advance at the appropriate level.'

questionBank.q: Approval requirements for a Risk Rating Limit Exception are determined by which factor?
opts: The tenor of the underlying facility only
The nationality of the obligor only

questionBank.q: A Cash Exception, as an RRLE type, refers to exceptions attributable to:
opts: Any facility priced below standard rate
Facilities to salary account holders only

questionBank.q: An 'Immaterial' Risk Rating Limit Exception is defined as an overage of up to what percentage of the Risk Rating Limit?
Passive exceptions may be caused by which of the following?
opts: A valuation change on an existing transaction, or a downgrade in the obligor's risk rating
A change of Relationship Manager on the account
A change in the customer's registered business address
The customer requesting a new chequebook
questionBank.ans: A valuation change on an existing transaction, or a downgrade in the obligor's risk rating

questionBank.q: Passive exceptions need not be pre-approved; instead, they are flagged as part of the regular reporting process and must be reviewed, with their action plan approved as soon as possible but no later than the next quarterly review of Risk Rating Exceptions
All RRLEs not captured under Cash, Immaterial, or Passive Exceptions are classified as:
Cash, Immaterial and Passive Risk Rating Limit Exceptions (RRLEs) require approval from which officers?
opts: Line ED and Chief Risk Officer (or their designees)
Line ED and Head of Credit Risk Management (or their designees)
questionBank.ans: Line ED and Chief Risk Officer (or their designees)

questionBank.q: All other Risk Rating Limit Exceptions, apart from Cash, Immaterial and Passive, require approval by which body?
An approved Risk Rating Limit Exception does not need to be re-approved during the Annual Review process, but must continue to be noted on the Facility Approval Memo
All Risk Rating Limit Exceptions will be reported quarterly to the Management Credit Committee
questionBank.exp: CORRECTION – section 5.3.5.8 states RRLEs are reported MONTHLY to the MCC, not quarterly.

questionBank.q: On what basis does the Chief Risk Officer review all Risk Rating Limit Exceptions, including exceptions that have aged past their originally established resolution period?
questionBank.exp: CORRECTION – section 5.3.5.8: CRO reviews RRLEs quarterly, not annually.

questionBank.q: A proposal or marketing letter does not require credit approval as long as it expressly disclaims any commitment or undertaking to provide a commitment or other services, and does not obligate Access Bank in any way
Marketing letters must be jointly approved by the Management Credit Committee and the Managing Director
questionBank.exp: False – section 5.3.6: 'Marketing letters will be jointly approved by the business head or ED and the Head of Risk.'

questionBank.q: Where a temporary overdraft (TOD) accommodation remains outstanding for longer than how many days shall it be classified as a Past Due Loan?
Any temporary accommodation that remains outstanding after 20 days shall be classified as a Past Due Loan
questionBank.exp: False – the correct threshold is 30 days, not 20.

questionBank.q: Temporary Overdraft accommodation shall be approved for not more than how many days per request?
questionBank.exp: Confirmed against section 3.6.4: TOD is approved for not more than 30 days per request.

questionBank.q: If an obligor's overdraft account shows no credits continuously for how many days (or credits insufficient to cover interest debited over that period), should the obligor be considered in default?
questionBank.exp: New question from section 6.4.21.1: default triggers after 90 days with no credits.

questionBank.q: May Access Bank increase an approved overdraft limit solely in order to avoid the facility being classified as default?
opts: No — enhancement in overdraft limits should not be approved just to avoid default classification
Yes, this is an accepted and encouraged practice for relationship management
Yes, but only for customers with a 10-year-plus banking relationship
Yes, provided the Board of Directors ratifies it retroactively
questionBank.ans: No — enhancement in overdraft limits should not be approved just to avoid default classification

What is the minimum tenor for loans under the Real Sector Support Fund (RSSF) via DCRR?
questionBank.exp: CPG (page 224) – RSSF requires minimum 7 years tenor.

questionBank.q: Under the Prudential Guidelines, what is the maximum total exposure (on and off balance sheet) by the bank to all tiers of government and their agencies?
Which of the following is a required element in an Offer Letter?
opts: Pricing information (including all fees) and conditions precedent to drawdown
Only the tenor of the facility
questionBank.ans: Pricing information (including all fees) and conditions precedent to drawdown
questionBank.exp: CPG (page 126) – offer letter must contain pricing and conditions.

questionBank.q: What is the maximum number of consecutive extensions permitted for a credit facility review?
questionBank.exp: CPG (page 63) – not more than 2 consecutive extensions.

questionBank.q: How often must the Bank conduct stress testing of its credit risk exposures?
opts: Only when required by the regulator

questionBank.q: Who must approve the issuance of a guarantee to support an offshore facility?
opts: The next higher level than required under the Credit Facilities Approval Grid
questionBank.ans: The next higher level than required under the Credit Facilities Approval Grid
questionBank.exp: CPG (page 34) – offshore guarantees require next higher level approval.

questionBank.q: Which of the following is NOT a recognised type of credit derivative for credit risk mitigation?
opts: Equity swap on the bank’s own shares
questionBank.ans: Equity swap on the bank’s own shares
questionBank.exp: Eligible credit derivatives are CDS, TRS, CLN, options – not equity swaps on own shares (page 184).

questionBank.q: Under the Prudential Guidelines, what is the minimum general provision required for outstanding credit facility balances not specifically provided for?
questionBank.exp: CPG (page 193) – general provision of at least 2%.

questionBank.q: What is the minimum number of years of audited financial statements required for a Tier I corporate borrower?
questionBank.exp: CPG (page 86) – Tier I requires minimum 3 years audited.

questionBank.q: What is the maximum allowed temporary overdraft (TOD) for value chain names with an ORR of Standard Grade?
questionBank.exp: CPG (page 121) – Standard Grade TOD limits: GM1 300mn, GM2 500mn, ED 700mn.

questionBank.q: What is the purpose of a "Covenant Check‑off List"?
opts: To be signed off by the officer responsible for reviewing all outstanding credit transactions and commitments at least annually
To list all customers with overdue loans
questionBank.ans: To be signed off by the officer responsible for reviewing all outstanding credit transactions and commitments at least annually
questionBank.exp: CPG (page 142) – covenant check-off list accompanies annual review.

questionBank.q: Credit Marketing, Credit Analysis and Packaging, Relationship Management, Credit Administration and Control and Credit Audit or Review are the 5 distinct phases in the Credit Management Cycle in Access Bank.
For Agricultural financing involving the acquisition of machinery and equipment, what minimum equity contribution is required as a condition precedent to drawdown?
opts: No minimum equity contribution is required
questionBank.exp: For financing involving the acquisition of machinery and equipment, a minimum equity contribution of 30% of the total cost shall be required (section 10.3.1).

questionBank.q: How often must the Agricultural Business Group carry out post‑disbursement site/farm visitation, and to whom is the report addressed?
opts: Semi‑annually, with a report prepared for the attention of the Head of Risk
Only once, immediately after disbursement, with no further visits required
Weekly, with reports sent to the Relationship Manager only
Annually, with reports sent to the Board of Directors directly
questionBank.ans: Semi‑annually, with a report prepared for the attention of the Head of Risk
questionBank.exp: The Agricultural Business Group must carry out post‑disbursement site/farm visitation semi‑annually and prepare a report for the attention of the Head of Risk (section 10.3.1).

questionBank.q: For agricultural financing, must Access Bank's general collateral requirements be supplemented with anything else?
opts: Yes — a comprehensive Agricultural insurance policy stating the Bank as first loss payee must be obtained
No, agricultural loans are exempt from all collateral requirements
Yes, but only a fire insurance policy is required, not a comprehensive agricultural policy
No additional requirement beyond the standard collateral checklist
questionBank.ans: Yes — a comprehensive Agricultural insurance policy stating the Bank as first loss payee must be obtained
questionBank.exp: In addition to meeting Access Bank's general collateral requirements, a comprehensive Agricultural insurance policy stating the Bank as first loss payee must be obtained (section 10.3.1).

questionBank.q: Which of the following is NOT a typical risk associated with Real Estate Project Finance?
questionBank.exp: Clearing Risk is a type of credit risk related to payment systems and is not a specific risk associated with Real Estate Project Finance. Construction, Compliance, and Environmental Risks are typical (section 10.7.5).

questionBank.q: For Real Estate Finance projects, the Bank will NOT finance:
questionBank.exp: Access Bank will not finance the cost of land, professional and other fees. Lending shall be used entirely to finance construction cost components (section 10.7.11).

questionBank.q: What is the minimum equity contribution for a Real Estate Finance project?
questionBank.exp: The borrower must have equity in the project of not less than 30% of the total cost, including land (section 10.7.11).

questionBank.q: What is the maximum loan tenor for direct loans to developers for financing housing estates (including any moratorium period)?
questionBank.exp: Direct loans to developers for financing housing estates will be for a period or tenor not exceeding five years (including any moratorium period) (section 10.7.16).

questionBank.q: In Project Finance, the primary source of loan repayment is:
opts: The revenues generated by the project itself
questionBank.ans: The revenues generated by the project itself
questionBank.exp: In project finance, the lender looks primarily to the revenues generated by a single project, both as the source of repayment and as security for the exposure (section 10.4).

questionBank.q: Which type of risk is mitigated by a fixed‑price, fixed‑delivery Engineering, Procurement and Construction (EPC) contract in Project Finance?
questionBank.exp: A General Constructor Agreement (or EPC contract) that provides a fixed price and a fixed delivery term is a key mitigant for Construction Risk (section 10.4).

questionBank.q: What is the minimum sponsor equity contribution required for a Project Finance loan?
questionBank.exp: The Sponsor has to ensure a minimum contribution of 20% to the project (section 10.4).

questionBank.q: In Project Finance, what is the purpose of a Debt Service Reserve Account (DSRA)?
opts: To build up a reserve to service debt in case of cash flow shortfalls
To pay for project operating expenses
questionBank.ans: To build up a reserve to service debt in case of cash flow shortfalls
questionBank.exp: A DSRA is built up to ensure debt service payments can be made even if project cash flows are insufficient (section 10.4).

questionBank.q: Which of the following is a typical security for Project Finance loans?
opts: Personal guarantee of the project manager
Letter of comfort from the government
A verbal undertaking from the sponsor
questionBank.exp: Project finance security includes assignment of operating revenues, mortgage on project facilities, pledge of bank accounts, etc. (section 10.4).

questionBank.q: In Object Finance, which of the following is a major risk that must be mitigated?
opts: Performance Risk (the object may not perform as expected)
questionBank.exp: Major risks in Object Finance include Performance Risk, Repayment Risk, Diversion Risk, and Tenor Mismatch (section 10.6.3).

questionBank.q: For Object Finance, what is the minimum equity contribution required from the customer?
questionBank.exp: Customer shall make an equity contribution of 10% to 30% depending on the risk profile of the obligor and the transaction (section 10.6.2).

questionBank.q: In Object Finance, a Marine surveyor report from an Access Bank approved Marine Surveyor shall be obtained as condition precedent to:
opts: Drawdown for vessels that are not brand new
review/analysis for vessels that are not brand new
Drawdown for vessels that are brand new
review/analysis for vessels that are brand new
questionBank.ans: review/analysis for vessels that are not brand new
questionBank.exp: Marine surveyor report from Access Bank approved Marine Surveyor shall be obtained as condition precedent to review/analysis for vessels that are not brand new (section 10.6.2).

questionBank.q: Under Object Finance, the Marine Survey report must state the following, EXCEPT:
opts: the date for the next special survey
the date for the next dry docking
Forced Sale Value of the vessel
questionBank.ans: Forced Sale Value of the vessel
questionBank.exp: The Marine Survey report must state the market value of the vessel, the date for the next special survey, and the date for the next dry docking. Forced Sale Value is not required (section 10.6.2).

questionBank.q: In Object Finance, the customer must have a minimum of how many years of proven experience in the type of contract to be undertaken?
questionBank.exp: Customer must have minimum of 5 years of proven experience in the type of contract to be undertaken (section 10.6.2).

questionBank.q: In Object Finance, can a second‑hand vessel be financed if it is free from encumbrance and fit for purpose?
questionBank.exp: Second hand vessel can be financed if it is free from encumbrance and fit for purpose (section 10.6.2).

questionBank.q: In Reserve Based Lending (RBL), which type of reserves does the Bank primarily lend against?
opts: Undeveloped reserves without any production history
questionBank.exp: The lending shall be restricted to Proven, Developed, and Producing (PDP) reserves (section 10.5).

questionBank.q: In Reserve Based Lending, the borrowing base is determined by:
opts: Technical valuation of the borrower's proved oil & gas reserves
questionBank.ans: Technical valuation of the borrower's proved oil & gas reserves
questionBank.exp: The borrowing base is determined by analysing previous production reports and independent engineering evaluations of proved reserves (section 10.5).

questionBank.q: In Reserve Based Lending, what is the purpose of a Competent Persons Report (CPR)?
opts: To provide an independent reserve valuation
To assess the borrower's management team
To confirm the borrower's tax status
To evaluate the political risk in the host country
questionBank.ans: To provide an independent reserve valuation
questionBank.exp: The Competent Persons report (CPR) shall contain sufficient information and documentation to support the assumptions and the analysis used to derive the forecasted cash flows and discounted PV (section 10.5).

questionBank.q: In Reserve Based Lending, how often is the borrowing base normally reset?
opts: Only at the inception of the loan
questionBank.exp: The borrowing base is normally reset every six months (section 10.5).

questionBank.q: In Reserve Based Lending, the Bank shall require an independent reserve audit every:
questionBank.exp: The revaluation of the reserves shall require an independent reserve audit company to prepare or audit the reserve reports and shall be conducted every 4 years from the date of first availment (section 10.5).

questionBank.q: Which of the following is a characteristic of Reserve Based Lending (RBL)?
opts: It is secured by liens on oil and gas mineral interests
It is based on the borrower's credit score
It is only for retail customers
questionBank.ans: It is secured by liens on oil and gas mineral interests
questionBank.exp: RBLs take the form of a borrowing base revolving credit facility secured by liens on oil and gas mineral interests (section 10.5).

questionBank.q: In Reserve Based Lending, how is the borrowing base deficiency typically cured?
opts: By the borrower adding additional oil and gas properties to the collateral base
By reducing the loan amount immediately
By the bank calling the loan
By the borrower issuing new shares
questionBank.ans: By the borrower adding additional oil and gas properties to the collateral base
questionBank.exp: The borrowing base deficiency shall be cured by the borrower adding additional oil and gas properties to the collateral base, or by monthly commitment reductions (section 10.5).

questionBank.q: Under the Mining lending framework, which team acts as the Centre of Excellence for coordinating lending activities to Mining companies?
opts: The Corporate Banking team in South Africa
The Head Office Credit Risk Management team
questionBank.ans: The Corporate Banking team in South Africa
questionBank.exp: The Corporate Banking team in South Africa will act as the Center of Excellence, responsible for coordinating the lending activities to Mining companies (section 10.10).

questionBank.q: For a Mining transaction, what must be in place before any lending is considered?
opts: A personal guarantee from the mining engineer
A letter of comfort from the host government
questionBank.exp: Mining Permit must be in place (section 10.8).

questionBank.q: Which of the following is an example of a government‑sponsored agricultural financing scheme mentioned in the CPG?
questionBank.exp: The CPG mentions CACS, ABP, AADS, Rice Distributors' Facility, Export Facilitation Initiative, etc. (section 10.3.5).

questionBank.q: What is the maximum loan limit under the Commercial Agricultural Credit Scheme (CACS)?
questionBank.exp: The SOL for CACS is set at N2 billion per project (section 10.3.5.1).

questionBank.q: What is the all‑in interest rate for loans under the Anchor Borrowers' Programme (ABP)?
questionBank.exp: Loans under the Anchor Borrowers' Programme are disbursed at an all‑in interest rate of 9% (section 10.3.5).

questionBank.q: Which of the following is an excluded project under the Agricultural Finance Policy?
opts: A project proposed by an unprofitable company
A project to finance the purchase of agricultural equipment
A project to finance an agro‑processing plant
questionBank.ans: A project proposed by an unprofitable company
questionBank.exp: Projects proposed by loss‑making or unprofitable companies are excluded (section 10.3.3).

questionBank.q: For Agricultural financing, what is the target market segment?
opts: Primary producers, agro‑processors, aggregators, exporters, agro‑input dealers, and agro‑mechanization
questionBank.ans: Primary producers, agro‑processors, aggregators, exporters, agro‑input dealers, and agro‑mechanization
questionBank.exp: The target market includes these value chain activities (section 10.3.2).

questionBank.q: In Project Finance, what is the purpose of a ‘Preferred Creditor Status’ protection?
opts: To obtain preferential treatment in case of country default
To mitigate transfer and convertibility risk
To bypass the Environmental Impact Assessment
questionBank.ans: To mitigate transfer and convertibility risk
questionBank.exp: Multilateral development banks (i.e. IFC, AfDB) “Preferred Creditor Status” protection mitigates transfer and convertibility risk for B Loan participants (section 10.4).

questionBank.q: In Project Finance, what is the typical maximum moratorium period?
questionBank.exp: Under the RSSF scheme, moratorium period is 2 years; generally project finance moratoriums are set based on project gestation, not fixed, but often up to 2 years (section 10.4).

questionBank.q: In Object Finance, the Bank shall ensure that the expiration of the certificate of class is at least:
questionBank.exp: Only vessels that are in class shall be financed. The bank shall ensure that the expiration of the certificate of class is at least 24 months (section 10.6.2).

questionBank.q: In Object Finance, the customer's contract must be a multi‑year time charter agreement – what is the preferred alternative if only a Letter of Intent (LOI) is available?
opts: Funding is still possible if there is a strong assurance of a firm contract within 6 months
LOI is never accepted under any circumstance
LOI is accepted only if the customer provides 100% cash collateral
LOI is accepted only for government‑backed charters
questionBank.ans: Funding is still possible if there is a strong assurance of a firm contract within 6 months
questionBank.exp: The use of LOI is strongly discouraged, but the bank shall consider funding on a case‑by‑case basis where there is strong assurance of a firm contract within 6 months (section 10.6.2).

questionBank.q: In Object Finance, what is the purpose of a Performance Bond (PB) from the ship builder (for new vessels)?
questionBank.exp: Performance Bond is a risk mitigant for performance, delivery, and collateral (section 10.6.3).

questionBank.q: In Object Finance, what is the maximum loan amount to one obligor (or group) as a percentage of the Bank's total shareholders' funds?
questionBank.exp: Financing of objects from one obligor (or a group of related obligors) shall not be more than 20% of the Bank's total shareholders’ funds (section 10.6.11).

questionBank.q: In Object Finance, the borrower must have a minimum of what percentage equity in the object's cost?
questionBank.exp: The borrower must have minimum of 10% equity in the object’s cost (section 10.6.11).

questionBank.q: In Real Estate Finance, which of the following is NOT a stage of risk associated with Real Estate Project Finance?
questionBank.exp: The risks are associated with scheme design, construction, and operation stages; syndication is a funding method, not a risk stage (section 10.7.5).

questionBank.q: In Real Estate Finance, the Bank shall not fund projects where the borrower is also the contractor, except under what condition?
opts: Where the borrower is an established real estate developer (exception requires one‑up approval)
Never, even if the borrower is a developer
Always, if the borrower provides a personal guarantee
Only if the project is below N1 billion
questionBank.ans: Where the borrower is an established real estate developer (exception requires one‑up approval)
questionBank.exp: The bank shall not fund projects where the borrower is also the contractor except where the borrower is an established real estate developer (exception to this shall require one up approval) (section 10.7.13).

questionBank.q: In Real Estate Finance, what is the maximum loan tenor for short‑term facilities?
questionBank.exp: Short‑term facilities shall be for periods not exceeding 2 years (section 10.7.16).

questionBank.q: What is the primary objective of the Bank's Environmental and Social Risk Management (ESRM) policy?
opts: To maximise lending to high‑risk industries
To ensure customers fulfil environmental and social responsibilities as part of loan obligations
To avoid any contact with government regulators
To reduce the number of loan applications
questionBank.ans: To ensure customers fulfil environmental and social responsibilities as part of loan obligations
questionBank.exp: The Bank shall insist on compliance with applicable National laws and regulations, the use of sound environmental, health & safety, and labour practices, as these are important factors in demonstrating effective corporate governance and ensuring commitment to loan obligations (section 11).

questionBank.q: Under the ESRM policy, which type of projects will the Bank NOT provide financial services to?
opts: Projects on the exclusion list of the ESRM Manual
Projects requiring an environmental impact assessment
questionBank.ans: Projects on the exclusion list of the ESRM Manual
questionBank.exp: The Bank shall not provide financial services to clients and projects / activities that are on the exclusion list of the Environmental and Social Risks Management (ESRM) Manual (section 11).

questionBank.q: The Bank's ESRM policy requires that all applicable projects be reviewed and approved in line with which documents?
opts: The Bank's CPG and ESRM Manual
questionBank.ans: The Bank's CPG and ESRM Manual
questionBank.exp: All applicable projects shall be reviewed and approved in line with credit processes as contained in the Bank’s CPG and ESRM Manual (section 11).
